questions.question: Which TWO of the following are Microsoft responsible AI principles?

options.why: Correct. Inclusiveness is one of the six principles.
Profitability is a business goal, not a responsible AI principle.
Correct. Accountability is one of the six principles.
Scalability is a technical quality, not a responsible AI principle.

questions.explanation: The six principles are fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.

questions.scenario: A bank discovers that its AI loan model approves applications from younger applicants less often than applications from older applicants who have the same income and credit history.
questions.question: Which responsible AI principle is the bank failing to meet?

options.why: Transparency concerns explaining how the system works. The issue described is unequal treatment.
Correct. Similar applicants receive different outcomes based on age.
The model operates consistently. The problem is that it treats groups differently.
No personal data is exposed in this scenario.

questions.explanation: Fairness requires that AI systems treat people in similar situations the same way.

questions.scenario: A medical chatbot must refuse to recommend medication doses and must direct users to a pharmacist when it cannot answer safely.
questions.question: Which responsible AI principle does this requirement primarily support?

options.why: Correct. The system must fail safely rather than cause harm.
Inclusiveness concerns making the system usable by everyone.
Accountability concerns who is answerable for the system, not how it responds to risky requests.
Fairness concerns equal treatment across groups.

questions.explanation: Reliability and safety requires an AI system to behave as intended and to fail in a safe way when it cannot help.

questions.scenario: A company requires that its customer-facing AI assistant displays a message stating that responses are generated by AI and may contain errors.
questions.question: Which responsible AI principle does this requirement support?

options.why: The message does not protect personal data.
The message does not affect how different groups are treated.
Correct. Users are informed that AI is used and that it has limitations.
Inclusiveness concerns designing for people of all abilities and backgrounds.

questions.explanation: Transparency means people know when AI is being used and understand its limitations.

questions.scenario: An organisation appoints a review board that must approve every AI system before release and investigate any harm the system causes.
questions.question: Which responsible AI principle does the review board address?

options.why: Correct. Named people are answerable for the design, release and outcomes of AI systems.
Transparency concerns explaining the system, not assigning responsibility for it.
Testing supports reliability, but assigning responsibility and oversight is accountability.
Inclusiveness concerns who can use the system.

questions.explanation: Accountability means people and organisations remain responsible for AI systems through governance and oversight.

questions.question: A voice assistant is redesigned so that users who are deaf or hard of hearing can interact with it by typing and reading captions. Which responsible AI principle does this change support?

options.why: Fairness concerns equal outcomes for similar people. This change concerns who can use the system at all.
Correct. The system is designed to work for people with different abilities.
The change does not affect data protection.
The change does not affect who is responsible for the system.

questions.explanation: Inclusiveness means AI systems are designed to engage and work for everyone, including people with disabilities.
